solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record boring speech in sketch?

indicators.note: a drill boring through something ends up sitting inside it

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone recording a dull talk and turning it into a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a verb, but it is the noun EP, drilled into DICTION to make DEPICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction is a portrayal or drawing, and a sketch is one kind; the question mark flags that it is an example.

clue.text: Stop woman coming out stark naked? There's no time

indicators.note: saying there is none of something means it must be removed from what is left

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman coming out into society

indicators.note: something naked is stripped of its covering, so the outer letters come off

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A scandalised plea to stop a debutante from appearing in society completely naked.
explanation.walkthrough: A deb is a debutante, a young upper-class woman formally 'coming out' into society; T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to prevent or prohibit them from doing something, so it is a verb synonym for stop.

clue.text: Department churning prosaic bulletin?

indicators.note: churning stirs things violently, so the letters get thoroughly mixed up

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An office that keeps churning out dull news releases, a gentle dig at the press office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the answer itself: a PR department churns out prosaic bulletins.
explanation.definitionFit: Public relations is the name of a company office or division that handles the organisation's image with the press.

clue.text: Lonely islander suggests reason for theatre closure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shipwrecked person stranded alone on an island
second meaning, read as two words: the actors have gone off, so no show can go on

explanation.surface: A marooned sailor somehow explaining why a theatre had to shut its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CAST AWAY and a theatre without its cast has to close; 'suggests' hints the second reading is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is someone shipwrecked and stranded, typically alone on a deserted island like Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Computer facility that connects circulating public transport with difficulty

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so letters are carried from the back round to the front

parts.note: a train is public transport
a net is a snare, a trap that puts its victim in difficulty

explanation.surface: A piece of computing kit that somehow links up a circling public transport system with great effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Circulating here means the tail of the word comes round to its head, two letters in this case. The net sense of difficulty is a loose one: a snare you struggle to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private computer network linking the machines and staff within one organisation.

clue.text: New wrestlers, having been exposed repeatedly, huddle together

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: exposing strips off a covering; done twice, two layers of outer letters come away

parts.note: strip the outer pair, then the next outer pair, leaving the core

explanation.surface: Novice wrestlers, having been repeatedly stripped, cluster together for warmth or comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: WRESTLERS loses W and S, then R and R, leaving ESTLE after N.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly or press close against others, which is what people do when they huddle together.

clue.text: God having care of particular Greek characters

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet; several of that one letter are mus

explanation.surface: A deity entrusted with looking after certain Greek people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek characters' suggests people, but it means letters of the Greek alphabet; 'particular' says they are all one letter, mu.
explanation.definitionFit: Comus is the minor Greek deity of revelry and festive excess, the subject of Milton's masque.

clue.text: Tetchy element of reviews received by Taxi Driver

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

indicators.note: an element is a single component, here a single letter taken from the start

parts.note: the initial letter

explanation.surface: Grumpy critics' comments about the Scorsese film Taxi Driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Taxi Driver look like the film title, but it is simply a cab driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby and tetchy are both adjectives for someone irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Unfortunate snag with failing gyms that could make bums look big

definitions.text: that could make bums look big

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters end up in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad-news gyms whose poor workouts leave your bottom looking larger.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a complaint about gyms, but it is literal: a lens enlarges whatever it is held over, bums included.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifying glass is a hand-held lens that enlarges the image of anything viewed through it.

clue.text: Energetic agent takes in both sides

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside yourself

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the two sides are right and left, the latter as L

explanation.surface: A lively double agent who plays for both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' suggests a double agent, but it supplies RIGHT and L to sit inside SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly is an adjective for someone lively and full of energy, especially an older person.

clue.text: Youngster's relations take charge for a while

parts.note: a baby is a youngster, with the possessive S
IT is slang for sex, as are sexual relations

explanation.surface: A child's relatives stepping in to look after things for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like relatives, but it means sexual relations, the old crossword IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after a child temporarily while the parents are out, a short spell in charge.

clue.text: Astonish excessively grand old actor

indicators.note: excess means one too many, so an extra letter is pushed in beside the one already there

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran performer
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A hammy veteran actor whose grandness is overwhelming enough to astonish.
explanation.walkthrough: STAGER already has one G; excess gives it a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to shock or amaze them so much they are almost knocked off balance.

clue.text: Side dish from Croatia ready on the counter

indicators.note: counter means contrary in direction, so the letters run backwards
taken from a phrase means lifted out of the run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A Croatian side dish sitting prepared on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a kitchen worktop, but it signals the letters are read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian yoghurt accompaniment, usually with cucumber and mint, served alongside curries.

clue.text: Bling (almost half diabolical) adapted for presenting off the cuff

indicators.note: half a word is its front portion, and almost trims one more letter from that
adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
its first half is DIABO; losing one more letter leaves four

explanation.surface: Flashy jewellery, somewhat hideous, altered to suit a presenter who improvises.
explanation.walkthrough: Bling is slang for showy jewellery; the bracket supplies four letters, mixed with the five of BLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbing means improvising words not in the script, and off the cuff is the idiom for unrehearsed speech.

clue.text: Ask Edgar about times past

indicators.note: about can mean around, turned in various directions, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and question a man named Edgar about history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dark Ages is the name for the early medieval period in Europe, a long-gone era of history.

clue.text: Nothing to stop dull sort of jazz being sent up in pub fixture?

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up means reading it from bottom to top
a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is jammed inside another

parts.note: drab means dull and colourless
O looks like zero
trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A pub band's dreary jazz being mocked, with nothing done to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: Trad is traditional jazz, the 1920s New Orleans style revived in Britain. 'In' is only a link here, not a container signal, and in a down clue 'sent up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is a fixed target hung on the wall of many British pubs for the game of darts.

clue.text: You once capsized, retreating to island

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so the letters are turned over

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned boating mishap, the capsized crew struggling back to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the two reversal words applies only to the short word next to it, so there are two separate flips side by side rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (or ait) is a small island in a river, a word used especially of islets in the Thames.

clue.text: Whenever required, having been reimprisoned, Republican's giving way to Democrat

indicators.note: giving way means stepping aside so that a replacement takes the place

parts.note: a prisoner sent back to custody awaiting trial is on remand
R is short for Republican
D is short for Democrat

explanation.surface: A US political story: a jailed Republican replaced by a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R of ON REMAND for a D. Being remanded means being returned to custody before trial.
explanation.definitionFit: On demand means available as soon as it is asked for, so at any time it is required.

clue.text: Mix kir with East European ale and North American water

indicators.note: mixing stirs ingredients together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation
E is short for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: blend kir with Eastern European ale and American water.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir is a white wine and blackcurrant drink; 'with' here is part of the recipe, joining pieces of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes, a body of fresh water on the US–Canada border.

clue.text: Bank on lady missing out on promotion

parts.note: re means on, as in regarding

indicators.note: missing out on something means going without it, so letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: Counting on a woman who was passed over for promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank on' is the natural phrase, but only 'Bank' defines; 'on' starts the wordplay as RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on or rely on something is to count on it; the definition is the verb bank in that trusting sense.

clue.text: Lumbering French unit get lamentably stoned

parts.note: un is French for one
to gain is to get

indicators.note: stoned fruit has its centre taken out, leaving only the outside

parts.note: only its first and last letters survive

explanation.surface: A clumsy French army unit getting sadly high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests a military unit but means the number one; 'stoned' suggests drugs but is the fruit sense, pitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly and lumbering are both adjectives for moving awkwardly and heavily, without grace.

clue.text: Go north to be introduced to crafty dwarf

indicators.note: being introduced into something means going inside it

parts.note: sly means crafty

indicators.note: heading north in a down entry means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate

explanation.surface: Travelling north to meet a cunning little man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' reads as travel but means relieve oneself; the result sits between SL and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White, so the dwarf is a named example.

clue.text: To some extent, marijuana use arouses aversion

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the text is used

parts.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A moral line: smoking cannabis provokes a degree of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the last two letters of the drug and ends on the first letter of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea can mean strong disgust or loathing, a feeling of revulsion toward something.

clue.text: Conflict and cut! … sums up the Iron Lady?

parts.note: a battle is a conflict
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Warfare and spending cuts summarise Margaret Thatcher's time in office.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Lady is Margaret Thatcher, UK prime minister 1979–90, known for the Falklands War and public spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle-axe is a formidable, domineering woman, a label often attached to Thatcher; the question mark marks her as an example.

clue.text: Wait for singer to ditch opening number

indicators.note: ditching an opening means throwing away the first letter
a singer produces sounds, so the word is taken by how it is voiced

parts.note: a heaviness word pronounced identically

explanation.surface: Holding on for a vocalist to drop the first song from the set list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening number' looks like a first song, but 'opening' is the first letter and 'number' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a numeral, one more than seven, so it is a straightforward example of a number.

clue.text: Society gallery closes in style

indicators.note: closing in on something surrounds it

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
S is short for society

explanation.surface: A fashionable club's gallery shuts down in grand fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closes' suggests the gallery shutting, but 'closes in' means surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste means discernment in matters of beauty and fashion, the sense of good style and elegance.

clue.text: Fuss about adult being excluded by Ra's worshippers

indicators.note: whatever is excluded is left out of the word

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing
re means about
the god's name with its possessive S
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A row over a grown-up being barred by followers of the Egyptian sun god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ra's worshippers' reads as a single idea, but Ra's supplies letters and 'worshippers' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorers are people who adore, and to adore originally meant to worship a god.

clue.text: Receivers of Iranian currency in deep water taking a turn

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
turning round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the deep is the sea
the rial is Iran's currency

explanation.surface: People handling Iranian money are in trouble, with events taking a bad turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receivers' suggests people accepting money, but they are radio receivers; 'in deep water' is not the idiom for trouble here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerials are antennae that pick up radio or television signals, so they are the devices that receive broadcasts.

clue.text: Old-fashioned levy charged by governments in the East

indicators.note: something charged is loaded or filled, so it holds another piece within

parts.note: a duty is a tax or levy

indicators.note: east is to the right on a map, so the rightmost letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: An outdated tax imposed by Asian governments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the East' sounds like Asia, but it points to the right-hand end of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty can describe something stale and outdated, as if it had been left unused on a shelf for years.

clue.text: Letter opener?

parts.note: surface reading: a knife for slitting envelopes
setter's reading: the person who opens a letter, being the one it was sent to

explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener is a desk tool, but the question mark allows a person who opens letters: the intended recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is written to is the one entitled to open and read it.
